The Idaho Transportation Department's (ITD) Roads and Highways Road Network Linear Referencing System (LRS) scenic byway event polyline feature class identifies the state's Scenic Byways, which are roads that have been designated for their outstanding scenic, natural, historic, recreational, archaeological, or cultural qualities, which are also known as \"intrinsic qualities\". These byways are recognized as gateways to adventure and offer a more immersive experience than a typical interstate, highlighting the unique character of the region. The term encompasses a collection of nationally and state-designated routes, often featuring special points of interest and interpretive information.<\/span><\/span><\/p>

This layer is an export from Roads and Highways that represents only the active records within the LRS.<\/span><\/span><\/p>

This content item is a sub-layer of the Road Network - Other<\/u><\/a> authoritative feature layer.<\/p>

This layer is a cartographic subset of BLM Arizona's Ground Transportation Linear Features (GTLF) dataset.<\/p>

The purpose of the Ground Transportation Linear Features (GTLF) data standard provides the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) with a better understanding of the impact of transportation on BLM programs. The national GTLF standard allows for the capture of data from the Travel Management Plan (TMP) as well as from observed route usage. The National GTLF data standard organizes GTLF data to meet National reporting requirements which typically are less detailed than field or State-level requirements. Therefore, individual states may extend the GTLF data standard domain lists to enhance data collection efforts. If the National GTLF data steward requires more detailed information about a particular State dataset, the National data steward will contact the appropriate state or field offices. The National BLM GTLF data standard is essential for collecting the landscape-scale data necessary to identify management opportunities and challenges that may not be evident when managing smaller land areas. GTLF data not only serve the crucial function of improving BLM transportation planning, but is also invaluable to numerous other BLM programs affected by transportation (e.g. water and air quality, wildlife habitat fragmentation, engineering, realty, cultural resources).<\/p>","tags":["Bureau of Land Management","BLM","Arizona","AZ","Freedom 250","Recreation","route","trail","back country byway"],"snippet":"Join the Freedom 250 celebration by experiencing the beauty, history, and adventure of Arizona\u2019s BLM-managed public lands","thumbnail":"thumbnail/thumbnail.png","documentation":null,"extent":[[-114.66963828546815,31.73924619021818],[-109.19617950514667,37.01161883896155]],"categories":["/Categories/transportation"],"spatialReference":"26912","accessInformation":"Bureau of Land Management, Arizona","classification":null,"licenseInfo":"
